subject: Mathematics
name: JHS 3 Mathematics
description: The JHS 3 Mathematics curriculum focuses on advanced number concepts including standard form, surds, and sets; algebraic proficiency in simultaneous equations, change of subject, and inequalities; geometric constructions and transformations like enlargement; and data handling including histograms and probability of dependent events.

strands.title: NUMBER
strands.description: Advanced number concepts, operations, and applications.

subStrands.title: NUMBER AND NUMERATION SYSTEM
subStrands.description: Standard form, significant figures, and set theory.

contentStandards.description: Apply the understanding of place value in solving real life problems involving integers of any size, rounding this to given decimal places and significant figures

indicators.description: Express integers to a given number of significant and decimal places

exemplars.description: Express integers to a number of significant figures.
Express decimal numbers to a given number of decimal places.

indicators.description: Use knowledge and understanding of place value to solve real life problems

exemplars.description: Create and solve a real-life problem or a story problem and write the answer in standard form.
Create similar real story problems and solve.

contentStandards.description: Demonstrate an understanding of the relationship between members of the rational number system and solve real life problems involving union and intersection of three sets

indicators.description: Solve problems on relationship between members of the rational number system using knowledge and understanding of the concept of union and intersection of two sets

exemplars.description: Use sets diagrams to show the relationship among the Real numbers namely Irrational, Rational, Integers, Whole, and Natural numbers.
Write the factors of numbers and represent them on a Venn diagram.

indicators.description: Apply the concept of sets to solve problems on relationship between members of rational number system and solve real life problems involving union and intersection of two sets

exemplars.description: Create and solve real life problems to show the union and intersection of two sets.

contentStandards.description: Apply mental mathematics and properties to determine answers for addition and subtraction of basic facts

indicators.description: Multiply and divide given numbers by powers of 10 including decimals and benchmark fractions

exemplars.description: Recall multiplication facts up to 144 and related division facts.
Recall decimal names of given benchmark fractions converted to decimals or percentages.
Find the product of a given decimal number when it is multiplied by powers of 10.

indicators.description: Demonstrate the ability to determine commutative properties of addition and multiplication

exemplars.description: Recognise that for any two numbers a and b; a + b = b + a and a × b = b × a.

indicators.description: Use the associative property of addition and multiplication

exemplars.description: Recognise that for any three numbers a, b and c; a + (b + c) = (a + b) + c and (a × b) × c = a × (b × c).

indicators.description: Use the distributive property in solving problems

exemplars.description: Recognise that for any three numbers a, b and c; a × (b + c) = (a × b) + (a × c) and a × (b - c) = (a × b) - (a × c).

contentStandards.description: Apply the understanding of addition, subtraction, multiplication and division of decimal numbers to solve problems, and round answers to given decimal places and significant figures

indicators.description: Solve operations involving addition, subtraction, multiplication and division using word problems

exemplars.description: Create and solve story problems involving a combination of two or more of the basic operations.

indicators.description: Solve word problems involving the four basic operations and round the answers to the nearest two decimal figures or to some significant figures

exemplars.description: Calculate total amounts in word problems and round answers to specified decimal places or significant figures.

contentStandards.description: Demonstrate understanding of surds as real numbers, the process of adding and subtracting of surds as well as determining (using a calculator) the approximate square root of a number that is not a perfect square

indicators.description: Identify simple and compound surds

exemplars.description: Identify examples of simple and compound surds.

indicators.description: Explain the identities/rules of surds

exemplars.description: Explain and use rules of surds for multiplication, division, and rationalization.

indicators.description: Simplify given surds

exemplars.description: Simplify surd expressions.

indicators.description: Approximate the square roots of non-perfect squares with calculators/tables

exemplars.description: Find square roots of non-perfect squares.

subStrands.title: FRACTIONS, DECIMALS AND PERCENTAGES
subStrands.description: Operations with fractions and solving related problems.

contentStandards.description: Apply the understanding of operations on fractions to solve problems involving fractions of given quantities and round the results to given decimal and significant places

indicators.description: Review fractions and solve problems involving basic operations on fractions

exemplars.description: Review the concept of fraction.
Review the basic operations on fractions (addition, subtraction, multiplication, division).

indicators.description: Add and/or subtract, multiply and/or divide given fractions, using the principle of order of operations including the use of the BODMAS or PEMDAS rule, and apply the understanding of these to solve problems

exemplars.description: Use the order of operations to simplify whole number expressions with more than two operations.
Use the order of operations to simplify fractions with more than two operations.

indicators.description: Review word problems involving basic operations on fractions

exemplars.description: Solve word problems based on fractions.

subStrands.title: NUMBER: RATIOS AND PROPORTION
subStrands.description: Solving real-world problems involving ratio, rate, and proportion.

contentStandards.description: Apply the understanding of ratio, rate and proportions to solve problems that involve rates, ratios, and proportional reasoning and use it to solve real world mathematical problems

indicators.description: Represent proportional relationships by equations

exemplars.description: Express relationships where total cost is proportional to number of items as equations.

indicators.description: Use proportional relationships to solve multistep ratio and percent problems, examples: simple interest, tax, discount and commissions, NHIL, depreciation, insurance, etc.

exemplars.description: Solve problems on simple interest.
Solve problems on tax (VAT).
Solve problems on discount.
Solve problems on commission.
Solve problems involving depreciation.
Solve problems involving NHIL.
Solve problems involving insurance.

indicators.description: Use knowledge of rates and proportional reasoning to solve problems involving SSNIT benefits and contributions

exemplars.description: Describe the obligations of the employer/employee and the contribution rates.
Calculate employee/employer contributions to SSNIT under Act 766.
Calculate employee/employer contributions to SSNIT under PNDCL 247.
Calculate employee benefits from SSNIT under Act 766.
Calculate employee benefits from SSNIT under PNDCL 247.

indicators.description: Recognise and graph proportional relationships, interpreting the unit rate as the slope of the graph and use these to solve problems

exemplars.description: Interpret graphs of cost versus quantity to find unit rates and solve cost problems.

strands.title: ALGEBRA
strands.description: Advanced algebraic concepts involving simultaneous equations, change of subject, and inequalities.

contentStandards.description: Demonstrate the ability to construct tables of values for pairs of linear relations, graph the relations in a number plane and determine the intersection of the lines to solve simultaneous linear equations

indicators.description: Construct a table of values for two linear relations and graph the relation

exemplars.description: Construct a table of values for two linear relations and draw the graphs.
Draw graph for two linear relations.
Construct a table of values for two linear relations.
Draw a graph for two linear relations.

indicators.description: Use graphs of two linear relations to determine subsequent missing elements in ordered pairs of the relation

exemplars.description: Find the missing elements of ordered pairs on graphs of two linear relations.

indicators.description: Use graphs to solve equations involving two linear relations

exemplars.description: Solve two linear equations simultaneously using the graph shown.
Solve two linear equations simultaneously using the graph.

subStrands.title: ALGEBRAIC EXPRESSIONS
subStrands.description: Change of subject, substitution, and factorization.

contentStandards.description: Demonstrate an understanding of (i) change of subject (ii) substituting values to evaluate expressions, and (iii) factorize expressions that have simple binomial as a factor

indicators.description: Perform change of subject of a given formula and use it to solve problems

exemplars.description: Perform change of subject for given formulae.
Use the concept of change of subject to solve problems involving formulae.

indicators.description: Substitute values into given formulae to evaluate it and use it to solve problems

exemplars.description: Substitute values into expressions to find their value.
Make a variable the subject and find its value.
Find volume using the formula for a cone.

indicators.description: Factorise expressions that have simple binomial

exemplars.description: Factorise expressions using common factors.

indicators.description: Use the knowledge of simplifying and factorising expressions to solve real world problems

exemplars.description: Solve problems involving capacity and number of items.
Solve money problems involving prices of items.
Solve area and dimension problems for rectangles.

contentStandards.description: Demonstrate understanding of single variable linear inequalities with rational coefficients including: solving inequalities, verifying, comparing, graphing

indicators.description: Solve single variable linear inequalities with rational coefficients

exemplars.description: Translate word problems into linear inequalities in one variable and vice versa.
Solve simple linear inequalities.

indicators.description: Illustrate solution sets of linear inequalities on the number line

exemplars.description: Illustrate and explain inequality signs.
Graph linear inequalities in one variable on a number line.
Solve and graph linear inequalities on a number line.
Solve and graph linear inequalities on a cartesian plane.

indicators.description: Solve real-life problems involving linear equations and inequalities

exemplars.description: Solve real-life problems involving linear equations.
Solve real-life problems involving linear inequalities.

subStrands.title: SHAPES AND SPACE
subStrands.description: Properties of angles, polygons, and constructions.

contentStandards.description: Apply the properties of angles at a point, angles on a straight line, vertically opposite angles, corresponding, angles to solve problems

indicators.description: Derive the formula for calculating the sum of angles in any polygon and use this to calculate the value of missing angles in polygons

exemplars.description: Identify and name the various polygons.
Derive and use the formula (n - 2) × 180 ° for triangles.
Derive and use the formula (n - 2) × 180 ° for quadrilaterals.
Derive and use the formula (n - 2) × 180 ° for polygons, pentagons, hexagons, etc.

indicators.description: Identify similar and congruent triangles and use the knowledge to solve related problems

exemplars.description: Recognise similar triangles and solve for values of angles.
Recognise congruent triangles and solve for values of angles.
Determine values of unknowns using similarity and congruency.

contentStandards.description: Construct inscribed and circumscribed triangles and parallelograms with given dimensions

indicators.description: Draw inscribed and circumscribed circles for triangles under given conditions

exemplars.description: Construct a triangle and locate the incentre.
Draw an inscribed circle in a triangle.
Construct a triangle and locate the circumcentre.
Draw a circumscribed circle for a triangle.

indicators.description: Construct parallelograms (i.e. square, rectangle, rhombus) under given conditions

exemplars.description: Perform geometric construction of a square with a given side.
Construct a square given a side and measure the diagonal.
Perform geometric construction of a square with a given diagonal.
Perform geometric construction of a rectangle with given side.
Perform geometric construction of a rectangle with a given side and diagonal.
Perform geometric construction of a parallelogram with given sides and given angle(s).
Perform geometric construction of regular compound plane shapes with given sides and angles.

contentStandards.description: Derive the formulas for determining the surface area of prisms (i.e. cuboid and triangular prism) and use to solve problems

indicators.description: Identify cuboids and triangular prisms; draw their nets to construct the 3-D shapes and use it to determine the surface area

exemplars.description: Sort out shapes that are triangular prisms and cuboids.
Identify nets of shapes.
Measure and find the area of each section in the net to find surface area.

indicators.description: Use the net of a cuboid to determine its surface area

exemplars.description: Find the surface area of cuboids.

indicators.description: Use the net of a triangular prism to determine its surface area

exemplars.description: Find the surface area of triangular prisms.

indicators.description: Express points in the Cartesian plane as position vectors

exemplars.description: Identity the origin and position vectors.
Draw and write position vectors of points.

contentStandards.description: Solve problems involving bearings and addition/subtraction of vectors

indicators.description: Show an understanding of parallel vectors and perpendicular vectors

exemplars.description: Investigate conditions for parallel vectors and perpendicular vectors.
Solve questions involving parallel and perpendicular vectors.

indicators.description: Apply the triangular and parallelogram laws of addition to resolve vectors

exemplars.description: Deduce the triangle law of vector addition.
Express vectors as column vectors, show isosceles property and find equations.
Investigate the parallelogram law of vector addition.
Find vectors in a parallelogram and values of variables.

contentStandards.description: Demonstrate understanding of how to perform an enlargement on a geometrical shape given a scale factor and describe the properties of the image under the transformation (i.e. congruence, similarity, etc.)

indicators.description: Know examples of situations in everyday life that depict enlargement situations in everyday life

exemplars.description: Know examples of situations that relate to enlargement situations in everyday life.

indicators.description: Understand enlargement and identify real-life situations involving enlargement

exemplars.description: Draw an enlargement of shapes using a given scale factor. State transformations mapping shapes. Investigate characteristics of enlargements under various scale factor conditions.
Determine the scale factor in a transformation.

indicators.description: Investigate the concept of congruent and similar shapes

exemplars.description: Verify congruent and similar shapes using their properties on a coordinate plane.

subStrands.title: DATA
subStrands.description: Data collection methods, histograms, and descriptive statistics.

contentStandards.description: Select, justify, and use appropriate methods to collect data (grouped/ungrouped), use the data to construct and interpret frequency tables and histogram and use it to determine the mode and to solve and/or pose problems

indicators.description: Select and justify a method to collect data (quantitative and qualitative) to answer a given question

exemplars.description: Discuss and decide on data collection methods for given scenarios.
Identify which method to use for gathering facts.

indicators.description: Organise data (grouped/ungrouped) present it in frequency tables, line graphs, pie graphs, bar graphs and/or pictographs (representations include infographics, waffle diagrams, box and whisker plots and stem and leaf plots) and analyse it to solve and/or pose problems

exemplars.description: Present raw data in a frequency table.
Determine modal group. Use stem and leaf plots to display data and solve problems (range, mode, median).
Use pictographs to answer questions and represent data with infographics.

indicators.description: Use a histogram to determine the mode of a given data to solve and/or pose real life cases

exemplars.description: Construct frequency tables using different class intervals and draw a histogram to find the modal class.

contentStandards.description: Select, justify, and use appropriate methods of collecting data (quantitative and qualitative), organise and analyse the data (grouped/ungrouped) to interpret the results using the descriptive statistics (measures of central tendency and range)

indicators.description: Select a method for collecting data (quantitative and qualitative), taking into consideration how bias (use of language, ethics, cost, time and timing, privacy or cultural sensitivity) may influence data

exemplars.description: Discuss bias in survey questions and suggest improvements.
Analyze influencing factors in surveys like time and bias.
Identify influencing factors and provide solutions.
Discuss ethics in data usage.
Discuss culturally sensitive questions.

indicators.description: Organise and analyse data and interpret the results using the descriptive statistics (i.e. minimum, maximum, measures of central tendency and range) to answer a given question

exemplars.description: Find minimum, maximum, range, mean, median, mode from data and make decisions.

indicators.description: Demonstrate the effect on the mean, median, and mode when extreme data is included in a data set

exemplars.description: Calculate and compare mean, median, and mode when extreme values are added or changed.

contentStandards.description: Identify the sample space for a probability experiment involving two dependent events and express the probabilities of given events as fractions, decimals, percentages and/or ratios to solve problems

indicators.description: Perform a probability experiment involving two dependent events e.g. drawing coloured bottle tops from a bag without replacement

exemplars.description: List elements of sample space for picking items without replacement and discuss dependence.

indicators.description: Express the probabilities of the events as fractions, decimals, percentages and/or ratios; e.g. using a tree diagram, table or another graphic organiser

exemplars.description: Draw probability tree diagrams and express probabilities.
Calculate probabilities of drawing cards without replacement.
